quizzes.title: Karbi Anglong and Workplace Rights
quizzes.passage:
Unrest in Karbi Anglong, the largest district of Assam, has renewed debate on land and resource rights. The current instability began with a hunger strike by indigenous tribal groups, who demanded the eviction of long-settled non-tribal communities. Protesters argue that these settlements in protected grazing and tribal lands are unconstitutional and illegal. The district is administered by an autonomous council that works under a constitutional scheme giving autonomy to tribal areas in the North-East. A tripartite peace accord signed in 2021 aimed to end decades of insurgency and promised the council greater legislative, executive and administrative powers.

Workplace rights are also under debate. A private member's bill introduced in the Lok Sabha seeks to give employees a statutory right to refuse work calls, emails or messages beyond working hours and on holidays. Such bills are introduced by MPs who are not ministers, and their passage is uncommon. Constant digital availability is linked to anxiety, sleep-related disorders and burnout.

Harassment complaints form another part of this debate. A Supreme Court judgment held that a woman can approach the Internal Complaints Committee at her own workplace when the harasser is an outsider. The ruling expands the jurisdiction of the law on sexual harassment at work, which is based on guidelines issued by the Supreme Court. Its aim is to prevent, prohibit and redress harassment, and it applies to all women irrespective of employment status.

questions.q: Under which article does the booklet say Parliament can create an 'Autonomous State' within Assam for certain tribal areas?
questions.explanation: Article 244(A) allows Parliament to create an Autonomous State within Assam for certain tribal areas.

questions.q: Which country's El Khomri Law (2017) was the first national law recognising the right to disconnect?
questions.explanation: France's El Khomri Law of 2017 was the first national law recognising the right to disconnect.

questions.q: In a workplace employing how many persons is an Internal Complaints Committee mandatory?
questions.explanation: An Internal Complaints Committee is mandatory in every workplace employing 10 or more persons.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December every year.
Reason (R): 10 December marks the 1948 adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Human Rights Day marks the adoption of the UDHR in 1948, so R correctly explains the date in A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Universal Declaration of Human Rights   ->   A. Formed in 2006 to replace the UN Human Rights Commission
II. Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights   ->   B. Criteria for effective national human rights institutions
III. UN Human Rights Council   ->   C. Not a legally binding treaty but forms the International Bill of Human Rights
IV. Paris Principles   ->   D. Established by the Vienna Declaration in 1993
questions.explanation: The UDHR is not legally binding, OHCHR was set up under the Vienna Declaration, the HRC was formed in 2006 and the Paris Principles set criteria for national institutions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. An Internal Complaints Committee is mandatory in every workplace employing 10 or more persons.
II. A Local Committee is constituted by the District Officer where an ICC is not available.
III. The Right to Disconnect was first recognised as a national law in Australia in 2024.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the PoSH framework, while III is wrong because France was the first country, in 2017.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is a legally binding treaty.
II. Members of the Human Rights Council are elected for three-year terms.
III. The Human Rights Council was formed in 2006.
IV. Council members can be immediately re-elected after two consecutive terms.
questions.explanation: Only statements II and III are correct, since the UDHR is not binding and members cannot be immediately re-elected after two terms.

quizzes.title: Assam ST Proposal and Labour Rights
quizzes.passage:
The Assam Group of Ministers has recommended Scheduled Tribe status for a group of communities, a move that would be a significant step toward inclusion for them. Scheduled Tribe status is granted to groups identified under the Constitution, and the President holds the authority to notify the initial list. Any later revision of that list needs approval from Parliament. The proposal would create a new category called ST (Valley), and all such communities would fall under a National ST List. Until formal approval, the ministers have suggested a temporary relief in the form of sub-categorising the existing OBC quota within the state.

The move is described as a major inclusion step, but it has not yet been formally approved. At present, Assam has two ST segments. ST (Plains) carries a reservation of ten per cent, while ST (Hills) carries a smaller share. The proposal is therefore significant for reservation policy in the state.

The debate on workplace rights has its own constitutional roots. A proposed Right to Disconnect is linked to the right to dignity and a life with meaningful rest. The Constitution also directs the State to protect workers' health and to create humane and safe working conditions. Such a law would give employees a statutory right to refuse work messages beyond work hours and on holidays.

questions.q: What reservation share, in per cent, does the ST (Hills) segment have in Assam?
questions.explanation: ST (Hills) carries a 5 per cent reservation, while ST (Plains) carries 10 per cent.

questions.q: Under which article is Scheduled Tribe defined as a group identified under Article 342?
questions.explanation: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes as groups identified under Article 342.

questions.q: How many communities did Assam's Group of Ministers recommend for ST status? (number)
questions.explanation: The Assam Group of Ministers recommended ST status for 6 communities.

questions.q: Under which article is the right to dignity and a life with meaningful rest placed, as cited for the Right to Disconnect?
questions.explanation: Article 21 ensures dignity and a life with meaningful rest, which is cited as backing for the Right to Disconnect.

questions.q: Under which article does the Constitution direct the State to prevent exploitation of workers' health?
questions.explanation: Article 39(e) mandates that the State prevent the exploitation of workers' health.

questions.q: In which country did a 2024 amendment to the Fair Work Act let employees decline after-hours work communications?
questions.explanation: Australia's 2024 amendments to the Fair Work Act allowed employees to decline after-hours work communications.

questions.q: Under which article does the President get the authority to notify the initial list of Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: Article 342 grants the President the authority to notify the initial list of Scheduled Tribes.

quizzes.title: Seismic Zones, Forests and Nuclear Bill
quizzes.passage:
India has updated its seismic zonation map under the Earthquake Design Code of 2025, factoring in fault lines, tectonics and historical earthquake data. The revised map places the entire Himalayan arc in a new highest-risk zone for the first time. Towns located on the boundaries between zones will now automatically fall into the higher-risk category. The approach shifts focus from administrative boundaries to geological conditions, with stronger emphasis on active faults and the behaviour of rock and soil. This matters because a large part of the population lives in seismically active regions.

Forests face a growing threat from fire. According to the India State of Forest Report 2021, over 36 per cent of forests are prone to frequent fires. Governments have responded with schemes that support states in managing forest fires. At UNEA-7 in Nairobi, India's resolution on strengthening global wildfire management was adopted.

Nuclear energy is also being reformed. A bill introduced in the Lok Sabha would open the sector to private companies and joint ventures with government entities. It would give the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board statutory status and create an advisory council to hear appeals against decisions of the Central Government and the regulator. Under the bill, the nuclear liability framework would move to a tiered structure based on reactor capacity.

questions.q: Before the revision, the Himalayan arc was split between which two seismic zones?
questions.explanation: The Himalayan arc was previously split between Zones IV and V before Zone VI covered it entirely.

questions.q: What percentage of India's population lives in seismically active regions?
questions.explanation: 75 per cent of India's population lives in seismically active regions.

questions.q: Which bill proposes to replace the Atomic Energy Act 1962?
questions.explanation: The SHANTI Bill 2025 would replace the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2023.
Reason (R): It was launched to celebrate 50 years of Project Tiger.
Choose the correct option.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The alliance was launched in 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Pink Fire Retardant   ->   D. Special container hung under a helicopter and filled from a water source
II. Bambi Bucket   ->   A. Comprehensive plan to manage forest fires across India
III. National Action Plan on Forest Fires   ->   B. Ammonium phosphate-based slurry designed to slow or suppress wildfires
IV. Forest Fire Prevention and Management Scheme   ->   C. Centrally sponsored scheme giving financial support to states
questions.explanation: Pink fire retardant is an ammonium phosphate slurry, the Bambi bucket is a helicopter-hung container, the National Action Plan is a comprehensive plan and the scheme is centrally sponsored.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National Center for Seismology operates the National Seismological Network.
II. The SHANTI Bill 2025 would replace the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010.
III. Appendix II of CITES lists species threatened with extinction where commercial trade is prohibited.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III describes Appendix I rather than Appendix II.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The United Nations Environment Assembly was established in 2012.
II. The International Big Cat Alliance aims to conserve seven big cat species.
III. CITES Appendix I species are regulated through controlled trade.
IV. CITES came into force on 1 July 1975.
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct, while III is wrong because Appendix I prohibits commercial trade.

quizzes.title: Big Cats, CITES and UNEA-7
quizzes.passage:
The International Big Cat Alliance is a multi-country coalition that aims to conserve the world's large wild cats. It was set up to mark a major anniversary of India's tiger conservation programme. Its implementing body is a national authority under the environment ministry, and its secretariat is based in New Delhi. Countries where big cats live are invited to join, and any member of the United Nations is eligible.

The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species is a legally binding agreement that regulates global trade in wild fauna and flora. It was signed in Washington, and it aims to ensure that trade does not threaten the survival of species. The agreement does not replace national laws, so countries must pass domestic legislation to enforce it. Its appendices divide species according to the level of trade control they need.

Wildfire management also features in global talks. The United Nations Environment Assembly held its seventh session in Kenya in 2025, with the theme of a resilient planet. At that session, India's resolution on wildfire management was adopted. It calls for early warning systems, community-focused alert mechanisms and joint frameworks for prevention and recovery. It also supports national and regional action plans for integrated fire management, and it encourages the sharing of best practices among countries.

questions.q: In which year was the International Big Cat Alliance launched?
questions.explanation: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2023 by India.

questions.q: Which national body implements the International Big Cat Alliance?
questions.explanation: The National Tiger Conservation Authority under the MoEFCC implements the alliance.

questions.q: In which year did CITES come into force?
questions.explanation: CITES came into force on 1 July 1975.

questions.q: In which year was CITES signed?
questions.explanation: CITES was signed on 3 March 1973.

questions.q: Which CITES appendix lists species threatened with extinction, where commercial trade is prohibited? (Roman numeral)
questions.explanation: Appendix I lists species threatened with extinction, and commercial trade in them is prohibited.

questions.q: In which city was UNEA-7 held in 2025?
questions.explanation: UNEA-7 was held in Nairobi, Kenya, in 2025.

questions.q: The International Big Cat Alliance was set up to celebrate how many years of Project Tiger? (in years)
questions.explanation: The alliance was launched to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Project Tiger.

quizzes.title: Vande Mataram, HIV and Heritage
quizzes.passage:
Parliament has scheduled a special discussion to commemorate 150 years of the national song, Vande Mataram. The song was composed as a patriotic response to the British promotion of a royal anthem. It was first published in a Bengali novel, and it later became the rallying cry of the Swadeshi movement after the Partition of Bengal. A decision of the Congress Working Committee in 1937 limited its national use to the first two stanzas, and that decision has been debated since. On 24 January 1950, the song was declared the national song, to be honoured equally with the national anthem.

Health policy is also part of this section. The National AIDS Control Programme aims at the prevention, control and management of HIV/AIDS in India. Its current phase is a central sector scheme that aligns with global development goals to end AIDS as a public health threat by a target year. Between 2010 and 2024, national HIV prevalence declined, and new infections fell sharply.

Heritage recognition also covers living traditions. Deepavali was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list, which seeks to safeguard knowledge, practices and traditions passed across generations. The list has categories such as oral traditions, performing arts, social practices and traditional craftsmanship. Such recognition is intended to ensure that these traditions continue to be practised.

questions.q: Vande Mataram was first published in which 1882 Bengali novel?
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was published in the 1882 Bengali novel Anandamath.

questions.q: Who declared Vande Mataram the national song on 24 January 1950?
questions.explanation: Dr Rajendra Prasad made the declaration on 24 January 1950.

questions.q: Unlike the national anthem, Vande Mataram is not enforceable under which Act?
options: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram is not enforceable under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971, unlike the national anthem.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Goa Liberation Day is observed on 19 December every year.
Reason (R): On 19 December 1961, Operation Vijay led to the liberation of Goa from Portuguese rule.
Choose the correct option.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Goa Liberation Day commemorates the 19 December 1961 Operation Vijay, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Atal Bihari Vajpayee   ->   D. Famous tune composed by Rabindranath Tagore
II. Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya   ->   C. Commemorates Operation Vijay of 1961
III. Goa Liberation Day   ->   A. Founder of Banaras Hindu University
IV. Vande Mataram   ->   B. Pokhran-II nuclear tests
questions.explanation: Vajpayee is linked to the Pokhran-II tests, Malaviya founded BHU, Goa Liberation Day commemorates Operation Vijay, and Vande Mataram's famous tune is by Tagore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 1937 Congress decision allowed all stanzas of Vande Mataram to be used at national gatherings.
II. Vande Mataram is enforceable under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971.
III. Deepavali was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2025.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement III is correct, since the 1937 decision limited national use to two stanzas and the song is not enforceable under the 1971 Act.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Atal Bihari Vajpayee was born on 25 December 1924.
II. Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya founded Banaras Hindu University.
III. Goa attained full statehood in 1961.
IV. India contributes about 5 per cent of the world's new HIV infections.
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct, while III is wrong because Goa attained full statehood in 1987.

quizzes.title: Leaders, Goa and NACP V
quizzes.passage:
Good Governance Day is marked on 25 December, the birth anniversary of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He served as Prime Minister for three terms and became the first non-Congress Prime Minister to complete a full term. During his government, India conducted nuclear tests, and a major highway project was launched to connect important cities. He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and later with the Bharat Ratna.

The same day honours Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, who was a Congress president on several occasions. He founded a university in Varanasi and a Hindi weekly named Abhyudaya. He was also associated with the Hindu Mahasabha, which he helped establish.

Goa's history is marked by a long period of Portuguese rule. After Indian armed forces acted in 1961, Goa, Daman and Diu became a union territory. Portugal later formally recognised Indian sovereignty over these territories through a treaty. Goa eventually attained full statehood, and it has since been one of India's states.

The National AIDS Control Programme is in its fifth phase, which is a central sector scheme. The phase aligns with a Sustainable Development Goal that targets ending AIDS as a public health threat. Between 2010 and 2024, national HIV prevalence declined, and new infections fell by nearly half. The programme is implemented by the National AIDS Control Organisation under the health ministry.

questions.q: In which year was Atal Bihari Vajpayee posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: Vajpayee was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2015.

questions.q: In which year did India conduct the Pokhran-II nuclear tests under Vajpayee's government?
questions.explanation: The Pokhran-II nuclear tests were conducted in 1998.

questions.q: In which year was Banaras Hindu University founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya?
questions.explanation: Malaviya founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916.

questions.q: In which year did Goa attain full statehood?
questions.explanation: Goa attained full statehood on 30 May 1987.

questions.q: In which year did Portugal formally recognise Indian sovereignty over Goa, Daman and Diu?
questions.explanation: Portugal formally recognised Indian sovereignty over Goa, Daman and Diu through a treaty in 1974.

questions.q: By which year does NACP V aim to end AIDS as a public health threat? (year)
questions.explanation: NACP V is aligned with SDG 3.3 to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

questions.q: How many times was Madan Mohan Malaviya President of the Indian National Congress? (number)
questions.explanation: Malaviya served as Congress President four times, in 1909, 1918, 1932 and 1933.
